sources.citation: Hercus, Luise A. 1986. Victorian languages: a late survey. Pacific Linguistics B-77. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: No Keramin/Kureinji/Yari-Yari material at all (grep of full text layer: zero hits); its stress sections concern Wembawemba, Wergaia and Madhimadhi.

sources.citation: McFarlane, [—]. 1886. No. 87. From Mallee Cliffs Station to Wentworth [Kemendok]. In E. M. Curr, The Australian race, vol. II, 282-284. Melbourne: Government Printer.
sources.note: Bare English-Kemendok wordlist 'hurriedly dictated' by the station owner; no pronunciation or accent remarks (archive.org scanned, checked pp. 282-284).

sources.citation: Cameron, A. L. P. 1885. Notes on some tribes of New South Wales. Journal of the Anthropological Institute of Great Britain and Ireland 14: 344-370.
sources.note: Ethnographic notes; section 10 'The Languages' (p. 365-367) gives a comparative table Keramin / Beri-ait / Barkinji with no pronunciation or accent remarks.

sources.citation: Jamieson, H. 1878. Mildura. Yerre-yerre Tribe [wordlist]. In R. Brough Smyth, The Aborigines of Victoria, vol. II, p. 74. Melbourne.
sources.note: Bare wordlist (Man Wir, Woman Coormup,...); no stress/accent remarks.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid pages nort2756, kera1256, kure1240, yari1243.
sources.note: Lists Horgen 2004, Cameron 1885, McFarlane 1886, Brough Smyth 1878 and Wafer & Lissarrague 2008: 26-29 as the references; no descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) reference typed.

sources.citation: Blake, Barry J., Luise Hercus, Stephen Morey & Edward Ryan. 2011. The Mathi group of languages. Pacific Linguistics 628. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Phonology chapter (incl. stress) covers Mathi-Mathi/Letyi-Letyi/Wati-Wati only (Southern Sunraysia). Keramin/Kureinyi/Yari-Yari appear only in the social-classification discussion (pp. 24-26: 'Yitha-Yitha, Tharti-Tharti, Keramin (Kureinyi including also Yari-Yari) and Ngintait') and in a few comparative forms; no stress statement for them.

sources.citation: Blake, Barry J. & Julie Reid. 1998. Classifying Victorian languages. In B. J. Blake (ed.), Wathawurrung and the Colac language of southern Victoria, 1-58. Pacific Linguistics C-147.
sources.note: Explicitly excludes Yitha-Yitha and Dardi-Dardi (p. 2) and has no Keramin content; its stress remark (pp. 12-13) is about Madhi-Madhi second-syllable stress.

sources.citation: Hercus, Luise A. 1989. Three linguistic studies from far south-western New South Wales. Aboriginal History 13(1): 44-62.
sources.note: Nothing on Keramin stress. Section 3b (pp. 57-58) groups Yitayita-Tartitarti with 'Keramin (including Kemendok and Yerre-yerre)', lists the only sources (Cameron 1884/85, Jamieson in Smyth 1878, McFarlane in Curr 1886) and compares wordlists. The one accent statement (p. 46) is about Mathimathi: 'a number of circumstances in which polysyllabic nouns have their main accent on the second syllable' - not this language.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0: Keramin (ER 2792) and Yari-Yari (ER 2778), contributor Erich Round, source 'Horgen nd'.
sources.note: Segment inventories only (23 segments each); no suprasegmental information. Establishes that Horgen's thesis contains a phonemic analysis of these varieties.

sources.citation: Wafer, Jim & Amanda Lissarrague. 2008. A handbook of Aboriginal languages of New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory. Nambucca Heads: Muurrbay Aboriginal Language and Culture Co-operative, pp. 26-29.
